deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is an archival cover sheet (wrapper) added later to the bundle. In ink: '6 Bl.' (6 leaves) at top right, and a heading line whose exact wording is uncertain. It ends '... an Weierstraß' or possibly '... Riemann'. In pencil: 'beide Blätter sind unzweifelhaft [underlined] von Weierstraß geschrieben. Göttingen 29.9.20 Schlesinger'. The signer is almost certainly Ludwig Schlesinger, who worked on Riemann/Weierstrass materials around 1920. The '100' at right is the folio number. The note asserts that the two enclosed leaves are undoubtedly in Weierstrass's hand, not Riemann's. Faint bleed-through from the next leaf shows the material concerned. It is an expression of the form S = (z-a_1)^{m_1} (z-a_2)^{m_2} ... (z-a_n)^{m_n}, a remark involving the sum (m_1+m_2+...+m_n), and an integral ∫ S(z,s) dz. This looks like the setting of Abelian or hypergeometric-type integrals of products of powers of linear factors. That content is not legible enough here to reconstruct, belongs to the following leaves, and per the note is by Weierstrass.

results.what: Archival attribution note: the enclosed two leaves are judged to be in Weierstrass's handwriting (Schlesinger, Göttingen, 29 Sept 1920).

deep.surprise_reason: Cover sheet with a 1920 provenance note and no mathematical content. Moreover, it states that the enclosed leaves are by Weierstrass, not Riemann.
transcription_corrections: The underlined pencil word is most likely 'unzweifelhaft' rather than 'eigenhändig': 'beide Blätter sind unzweifelhaft von Weierstraß geschrieben.'

The first (ink) line is uncertain. The reading 'Nachschrift Riemann an Weierstraß' is doubtful. Its last word does appear to be 'Weierstraß' (or possibly 'Riemann'), but the opening words are not securely legible.
